source.title: The Five-Year Prospective Study of Quality of Life in Hemifacial Spasm Treated with Abo-Botulinum Toxin A

authoritative_validator_execution.mode: exact supplied source files copied byte-for-byte into temporary import package

semantic_spot_checks.claim: The study enrolled and analyzed 74 HFS patients (56 female, 18 male).
Overall SF-36 rose from 57.4 ± 2.4 at baseline to 61.3 ± 3.0 at 27 months and declined to 52.1 ± 4.2 at 54 months (p=0.002).
The general-health subdomain improved across five years (p=0.02), while several other annualized SF-36 domains worsened at years 4-5.
CES-D did not significantly improve in sequential analysis (p=0.924).
Abo-BTX A was administered as 100 units IM every three months, 25 units at each of four facial sites.

extraction_limitations: The source does not report visit-specific denominators/attrition in the Results text.
The article does not provide dedicated adverse-event incidence data or neutralizing-antibody testing.
The Results narrative contains a likely labeling inconsistency at the 45-month 15.9 ± 2.3 value; the atom preserves and tags this source inconsistency rather than silently correcting it.
